Il primo pensiero è andato ai cambi. Per: Our first thought went to exchange rates. To know what a dollar is worth you shouldn't have to wait for the day's rate: we looked for the freshest free source and found it in Yahoo Finance, which gives the rate updated to the second; the ECB remains the official fallback and provides the history for the charts. We had also considered the OANDA website, but it has no free API and its terms forbid reading rates with a program, so we left it aside. The same near real-time rate is now also used to convert foreign-currency prices, so price and exchange rate are from the same moment.

A fund merger that was later cancelled, and some sales that were cancelled and redone, were being read as real sales: one row was enough to make a loss appear that never existed. Now those rows offset each other and do not count as sales, and the fix also applies to capital gains and closed positions. It proves that numbers must be checked every time, not just once.
